rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the 12-month CPI change; no increase if CPI is negative. Owners must give written notice of the ordinance at lease start or with any rent increase notice. The cap for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027 is 2.87%.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (Rent Stabilization Ordinance, adopted 2021)
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period
rules.effective_date_note: Per the city's adoption announcement (D085), ordinances not effective until Nov. 19, 2021; the city publishes the allowable increase by June 30 each year, effective Sept. 1.
rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after Feb. 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after Jan. 1, 1990. Owners may petition for fair-return relief.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential buildings constructed on or before Feb. 1, 1995.
rules.interaction: Local cap applies instead of the state cap where both cover a unit.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner petition for fair return relief

rules.review_note: No ordinance number or code section is given in the documents, so the citation is descriptive.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may not end a tenancy without a just cause stated in a written notice, and must first give notice of a curable violation. For no-fault terminations the owner must give 3 months of relocation assistance or waive the last 3 months of rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days; 3 months relocation assistance for no-fault
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, adopted 2021)
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice
rules.effective_date_note: Per the city's adoption announcement (D085); owners had to notify existing tenants before Dec. 19, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.interaction: Local ordinance governs instead of the state just-cause law where both apply.
rules.review_note: No ordinance number or code section is given in the documents, so the citation is descriptive.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, license or provide, algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data for Santa Ana residential rentals. Tenants can sue for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation per month, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.effective_date_note: Law-firm alert (D002/D037) states effective April 2, 2026; news items (D086, D087) describe first reading Feb. 17 and final vote March 3, 2026 without an effective date.
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 per violation per month; injunctive relief, damages, attorney's fees
rules.exemptions: Software relying solely on public data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.

unverifiable_exemptions: tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements

rules.review_note: Only secondary sources available; ordinance text not provided.

parsed.notes: Santa Ana: three rules consolidated (rent stabilization, just cause, algorithmic ban NS-3090). Documents say nothing about city-level security deposit, screening fee, or screening restriction rules, so no records or no-rule findings were made for those.
